_meta.source: Derived from the build-time global data-sourcing research (Suffix / Exchange / Currency Mapping Table + Empirical Yahoo Coverage Matrix), which in turn cites the build-time live IBKR probe for all IBKR-side facts. Entries marked verified:true were literally observed in the IBKR probe’s search_contracts output; verified:false entries are standard public IBKR convention, never observed in either probe session, and must be spot-checked with a live search_contracts call before being trusted in skill logic.
_meta.warning: IBKR exposes NO currency field anywhere in search_contracts/get_price_snapshot/get_price_history (the IBKR probe, verbatim: "No `currency` field anywhere in the snapshot response."). Every trading_currency value below is therefore an INFERENCE from the exchange, not an IBKR-confirmed fact — this inference is exactly what the skill's reconciliation gate (references/05-ibkr-handoff.md) tests on every trade candidate by cross-checking the currency-normalized price against Yahoo's live quote.currency. Do not treat this file as ground truth without that runtime cross-check.
_meta.minor_unit_convention_note: Yahoo's documented convention: a currency code ending in a lowercase letter after otherwise-uppercase ISO letters (e.g. "GBp") denotes minor-unit (subunit) quoting — divide by the stated divisor before use. Only "GBp" was empirically observed live in the source session (SHEL.L, ULVR.L). The existence of other minor-unit codes (e.g. "ZAc" for Johannesburg cents, "ILa") is general convention knowledge cited in the source, NOT independently re-verified — none of those markets are in this file's coverage, and none should be assumed minor-unit without live verification of the exact currency string.
_meta.lot_size_note: lot_size is null everywhere in this file. Neither source document establishes a numeric lot/board-lot size for any market — the build-time research mention that Japan and Hong Kong conventionally use non-1 round lots / board lots (referenced from SKILL.md's 08-multi-currency.md, which was not provided as a source for this file) but no exact unit count was observed or cited in the two documents this file is built from. Do not invent a number — verify via a live IBKR contract-details call before sizing any order in an affected market.

markets.notes: Baseline market. Empty Yahoo suffix = bare US ticker. Multiple IBKR exchange codes are valid depending on the specific primary/alternate listing venue; all four were directly observed in the IBKR probe’s search_contracts output.

.TO.notes: Some Canadian names dual-report financials in USD (empirically observed: Shopify/SHOP.TO — CAD shares, USD financialData.financialCurrency) even though shares trade in CAD. Always check financialData.financialCurrency separately from quote.currency; do not assume CAD financials from a CAD-quoted listing.

.L.trading_currency: GBp (pence) for most equities — confirmed live for SHEL.L and ULVR.L; GBP (pounds) also occurs on the same suffix for some ETFs/gilts
.L.notes: #1 trap in the whole dataset. Yahoo's currency field literally returns the string "GBp" (lowercase p) for penny-quoted LSE equities — the actual price is regularMarketPrice / 100 in pounds. "GBP" (all caps) is a DIFFERENT, also-valid Yahoo currency code used for some GBP-denominated ETFs/gilts on the same .L suffix. Never assume minor-unit quoting from the suffix alone — read the exact quote.currency string for every instrument, every time, per the skill's mandatory rule. minor_unit=true/divisor=100 here reflects the majority (equity) case only.

.IR.notes: Inferred. Yahoo confirms "ISE" as quote.exchange / fullExchangeName "Irish", which matches the IBKR probe’s IBKR country_code "IE" convention, but the IBKR probe never actually searched an Irish name via search_contracts — spot-check before trusting in skill logic.

.AS.notes: Yahoo's own exchange short code is "AMS", not "AEB" — Yahoo and IBKR use genuinely different short codes for the same venue. Never pass one system's exchange code to the other's API.

.DE.notes: IBIS is the IBKR probe’s primary observed Xetra code; FWB/FWB2 (Frankfurt floor) are alternate codes cited in the data-sourcing research but not independently confirmed as separately observed in the IBKR probe’s raw output — treat as unverified until spot-checked. Yahoo's own exchange short code is "GER", displayed name "XETRA" — a third, different short code from IBKR's.  Never pass one system's exchange code to the other's API.

.PA.notes: Yahoo's own exchange short code is "PAR" — different from IBKR's "SBF". Never pass one system's exchange code to the other's API.

.SW.notes: One of the few venues where Yahoo's own exchange code ("EBS") and IBKR's exchange code coincide — do not generalize this coincidence to other exchanges in this table; every other row here has been observed to differ between the two systems.

.MC.notes: Inferred, not observed in either probe session — spot-check before trusting. Financial-statement-history modules (incomeStatementHistory/balanceSheetHistory/cashflowStatementHistory) were EMPTY for the one Spanish name tested (Inditex, ITX.MC) despite summaryDetail/defaultKeyStatistics/financialData all being populated on the same call. Verify per-name before relying on IS/BS/CFS history for Spanish names; treat an empty result as "no data", not an error to retry.

.MI.notes: Inferred, not observed in either probe session — spot-check before trusting in skill logic.

.OL.notes: Inferred exchange code, not observed in either probe session. Observed financialData.financialCurrency="USD" for Equinor (EQNR.OL) despite NOK-quoted shares — oil/gas majors commonly report financials in USD regardless of home listing currency. Do not assume Nordic-listed names report financials in the Nordic trading currency; always check financialCurrency separately.

.T.notes: JPY has no minor/decimal subunit, so there is no GBp-style trap here — but nominal prices are very large; sanity-check magnitude, not currency identity. Japanese equities are conventionally traded in non-1 "round lots" — the exact unit is NOT established by either source document behind this file; verify via a live IBKR contract-details call before sizing an order, do not assume 100 or any other number. Separately (unrelated to lot size): Japanese GAAP (J-GAAP) still amortizes goodwill over up to 20 years, unlike IFRS/US GAAP — check accounting regime per Japanese company before trusting net-income-based multiples (see withholding-tax.json's sibling normalization notes / the IBKR probe fundamentals research).

.HK.notes: Inferred exchange code, not observed in either probe session. Observed financialData.financialCurrency="CNY" for Tencent (0700.HK) — mainland-China-domiciled issuers listed in HK commonly report financials in CNY/RMB while shares trade in HKD; do not assume "Hong Kong listing implies HKD financials." HK uses non-1 "board lots" that vary per security — exact unit not established by either source document; verify via a live IBKR contract-details call before sizing.

.AX.notes: Observed financialData.financialCurrency="USD" for BHP (BHP.AX) — large diversified miners with US-dollar-denominated global operations frequently report in USD despite an ASX-primary, AUD-quoted listing. Also see withholding-tax.json: Australian franking credits mean headline dividend yield is not a reliable after-tax proxy for this market.

.SI.notes: Inferred exchange code, not observed in either probe session. Financial-statement-history modules were EMPTY for the one Singaporean name tested (DBS, D05.SI) despite summaryDetail/defaultKeyStatistics/financialData all being populated — same caveat as .MC (Spain) above; verify per-name.

.KS.notes: No specific trap flagged in the source session beyond the general rules (always read quote.currency live, never assume from suffix).

.TW.notes: Inferred exchange code, not observed in either probe session — spot-check before trusting in skill logic. Separately (dividend, not exchange-code, trap): the US has NO income tax treaty with Taiwan at all — see withholding-tax.json, this is a structural withholding-drag trap distinct from the exchange-code uncertainty here.
